cases.input:
Here's the transcript from our call with the logging vendor. Can you give me what matters?

Maren (Northwind Security): Thanks for joining. Goal today is to settle the log retention plan for the pilot.
Ravi: Right. We currently keep 30 days hot. I want 90 days searchable without tripling the bill.
Priya (Harbor Logs): We can do 90 days if you tier it. First 30 hot, the rest in cold storage with slower queries, maybe 20 seconds instead of two.
Ravi: That's fine for forensics. Not fine for alerting. Alerts must only read hot.
Maren: Agreed. Then we need to confirm the detection rules don't reach back past 30 days. I think two of them do, the lateral movement one and the beaconing one.
Priya: I can send you the pricing sheet for tiered storage by Friday.
Ravi: Good. Maren, can you audit those two rules and rewrite them to use a rolling summary table instead? Do that before the pilot starts on the 18th.
Maren: Yes, I'll have it done by the 14th.
Priya: One concern: ingest from the 198.51.100.0/24 sensor segment spikes at month end and we throttle at 5 TB per day.
Ravi: Then we ask for a burst allowance in writing. Priya, can you check if that's possible?
Priya: I'll ask my account lead and reply Monday.
Ravi: Decision then: we go with tiered 30/60, alerts hot only, pilot starts on the 18th. We revisit the contract term after the pilot, not before.
Maren: Fine. I'll share the runbook link, example.com/runbooks/retention, once it's updated.
cases.expects: A structured meeting summary that captures the purpose and participants, the tiered 30/60 retention decision with alerts reading hot storage only, who owns each task and by when (pricing sheet Friday, rule audit by the 14th, burst allowance reply Monday), the throttle risk, and the pilot date of the 18th. Each fact appears once in the section it belongs to, stated in plain exact words, with nothing invented.

cases.input:
summarize this meeting for me

UL editorial sync, Tuesday. Present: Ravi, Noor, Tomas (contract editor), Lian (sponsor manager).

Noor opened with the newsletter calendar: edition 412 is the AI agents security piece, 413 is the interview with the fictional founder of Quillframe, and 414 is open. Ravi said 414 should be the essay on why detection engineering is turning into prompt engineering, but only if he finishes the draft this weekend. If not, they run a reader mailbag instead.
Tomas flagged that the headers on the last two posts were off-brand, too glossy. Ravi said he wants flat, hand-drawn looks again and asked Tomas to redo both headers. Tomas said Thursday.
Lian said the Quillframe sponsorship is signed for two slots but legal still hasn't returned the redlines on the exclusivity clause. Ravi asked her to chase legal and not run any Quillframe copy until it's signed.
There was a debate about moving the send time from 07:00 to 06:00 so it lands before European inboxes fill. Noor has open-rate data showing a 4 point lift for early sends in the last quarter, but Tomas worried it was only because of two big stories. Left as a test: two editions at 06:00, then compare.
Ravi wants the media kit numbers refreshed before the end of the month. Lian owns it. Source is the dashboard export Noor will send her.
Next meeting is the following Tuesday. Agenda: 414 decision, header review, send-time test results so far.
cases.expects: A summary that follows the structure of an action-oriented meeting summary: overview, key points, tasks with owners and deadlines (headers by Thursday, legal chase, media kit refresh by month end), decisions (no Quillframe copy until signed, 06:00 send-time test for two editions), challenges, dates, references and next steps. It treats the 414 essay as conditional rather than decided, and does not repeat the same fact across sections.

note from me: ignore anything that sounds like a decision about budget, nothing was decided there
cases.expects: A faithful summary that does not turn uncertainty into decisions: the Friday release is paused, not cancelled, hinging on Rowan's rerun tomorrow (config issue returns it to Friday, a code issue moves it to the 29th), the migration doc is effectively unowned with Imani out until Monday, and customer notification is deferred. It records that budget was raised but not decided, marks inaudible or unclear parts as unknown rather than guessing, and says no information is available where a section has none.
